Required evidence before implementation: Seed names, image paths, and application IDs with unique sensitive sentinels. Under minimal mode, no sentinel reaches inserted rows or API responses, including after an update and migration. Status filtering, missing-pod tracking, pagination, and aggregate metrics remain usable.

Feedback: Qualify privacy guarantees by storage surface and field origin. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid collecting more sensitive data to power privacy features. Do not add central raw-log archives, SQL capture, environment snapshots, or third-party scanning uploads solely to support redaction or troubleshooting. Preserve the current metadata boundary and operate on explicitly selected local excerpts; otherwise a privacy improvement creates a larger retention and access problem.

docs.title: 26.1 · Ship a small recorder-health dashboard and alert recipe
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Metric semantics are clarified at HELP and in documentation. Dashboard/failure taxonomy expansion needs operator use cases and a stable bounded vocabulary.

Required evidence before implementation: Against fixture time series, healthy collection stays green; age -1 alerts only after startup grace; stale age and failed scrapes produce different alerts; history-disabled deployments do not produce recorder-failure alerts. A documented example connects without embedding a token in URLs or dashboard files.

docs.title: 26.2 · Expose bounded collector failure reasons and collection timing
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Metric semantics are clarified at HELP and in documentation. Dashboard/failure taxonomy expansion needs operator use cases and a stable bounded vocabulary.

Required evidence before implementation: Inject representative timeout, denied-access, repeated-cursor, and storage errors and verify stable categories and duration measurements. Assert that arbitrary exception strings, application IDs, and pod names never create labels, and that worker takeover does not double count committed attempts.

Feedback: Make retained-count semantics explicit at the metric itself. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid per-application Prometheus labels or a competing Spark telemetry store. Application IDs, pod UIDs, SQL, and exception strings introduce unbounded cardinality and privacy exposure. Keep aggregate operational metrics bounded; use existing run identifiers for explicit drill-down and external Spark telemetry for execution detail.

docs.title: 27.1 · Show when diagnostic evidence happened and refresh successful snapshots
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Timestamp and cause-specific guidance are implemented. New command-generation or evidence collection UI should preserve the existing read-only boundary.

Required evidence before implementation: Fixtures containing an old scheduling warning, a current waiting state, a previous OOM and missing event times remain distinguishable in JSON and the panel. Refreshing a successful snapshot visibly advances collection time. In a small internal triage exercise, responders can identify evidence age without a separate Kubernetes query.

docs.title: 27.2 · Turn diagnostic next steps into scoped, read-only investigation recipes
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Timestamp and cause-specific guidance are implemented. New command-generation or evidence collection UI should preserve the existing read-only boundary.

Required evidence before implementation: Generated recipes consistently include the selected context, namespace and container, contain only allowed inspection operations, and quote arguments safely. In a staged crash-loop exercise, a responder retrieves the intended container's previous attempt within two minutes without editing resource identifiers.

Feedback: Make incomplete-report guidance specific to the missing evidence. Incomplete guidance distinguishes bounds, ownership, authorization, missing resources and transient failures. Diagnostics record collection time. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid automatic restart or resubmit buttons derived from diagnostic classifications. An observed crash, OOM or scheduling warning does not establish that replay is safe or that configuration changes are correct. Keep diagnosis as evidence-led investigation; application owners must decide recovery using checkpoint, idempotency and downstream-write knowledge the snapshot does not contain. This protects the useful narrow scope of the existing diagnostics and metadata history.

docs.title: 28.1 · Add a verified, portable history backup command
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. A consistent SQLite backup recipe and recovery coverage are documented. Automated restore/PVC drills require an explicitly selected deployment and backup destination.

Required evidence before implementation: While snapshots are being committed, create a backup and restore it into an isolated directory. Integrity validation passes and its rows form a transactionally consistent snapshot. Interrupting backup leaves no published successful artifact; using the live database as destination is rejected. A documented restore produces queryable records after restart.

docs.title: 28.2 · Provide a rehearsable PVC replacement and recovery playbook
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. A consistent SQLite backup recipe and recovery coverage are documented. Automated restore/PVC drills require an explicitly selected deployment and backup destination.

Required evidence before implementation: A maintainer follows the recipe on a disposable cluster, replaces the original claim, retrieves a retained completed run, observes fresh collection, and rolls back successfully. The resulting report distinguishes recoverable backup age from runs never observed or already pruned and records measured downtime.

Feedback: Describe recovery coverage separately from persistent storage. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Do not turn recorder durability into an HA database project. Retain the single-pod SQLite boundary. Shared-network-file replication or a new distributed database would add substantial migration and support obligations to an optional metadata recorder. Establish verified backups and rehearsed recovery first; require demonstrated demand before considering a different persistence architecture.

docs.title: 29.1 · Make internal service DNS use a configurable cluster domain
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Gateway acceptance is documented. Custom DNS/CONNECT proxy support changes routing and credentials and needs a concrete deployment fixture.

Required evidence before implementation: With clusterDomain set to corp.internal, render the chart and assert its History Server host ends in svc.corp.internal; capture a mocked Spark UI request and assert the same suffix. Default-domain outputs remain unchanged, and malformed domains fail configuration validation.

docs.title: 29.2 · Offer explicit CONNECT-proxy transport for remote submissions
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Gateway acceptance is documented. Custom DNS/CONNECT proxy support changes routing and credentials and needs a concrete deployment fixture.

Required evidence before implementation: A local test proxy records CONNECT to the configured API authority; a mock HTTPS API receives the bearer token only within the TLS tunnel. Invalid destination certificates fail, stalled tunnels time out, redirects remain refused, and setting HTTP_PROXY alone leaves direct-mode behavior unchanged.

Feedback: Turn gateway requirements into a verifiable deployment contract. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Do not become a service-mesh controller. Keep mesh certificate issuance, sidecar lifecycle, ingress-controller installation, and vendor-specific authorization policy with the platform owner. Small configuration hooks and verifiable examples preserve compatibility without promising a maintained matrix of mesh products. Do not solve private-network friction by disabling TLS verification or broadly allowing all egress.

docs.title: 30.1 · Expose a safe storage inventory in offline application plans
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Storage ownership and demo limits are documented. Inventory/classification expansion needs validated CSI/PVC examples; no automatic PVC cleanup.

Required evidence before implementation: Fixtures covering an embedded executor template, SDK volume settings, driver template, explicit Spark overrides, and an external template produce the expected inventory; external information remains explicitly unknown. Secret sentinel strings never appear, and offline planning makes zero Kubernetes calls.

docs.title: 30.2 · Add storage-specific diagnoses from existing pod and event evidence
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Storage ownership and demo limits are documented. Inventory/classification expansion needs validated CSI/PVC examples; no automatic PVC cleanup.

Required evidence before implementation: Representative event/status fixtures yield the correct storage code and actionable remediation; ambiguous evictions remain unclassified as storage. Existing diagnosis fixtures retain their results, collection request counts stay unchanged, and incomplete evidence remains visible.

Feedback: Keep the shared-PVC starter visibly scoped as a functional demo. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid automatic PVC garbage collection based only on application labels. Shared dataset volumes and reusable scratch volumes can outlive one application. The current generic volume inputs do not establish ownership or retention intent. A cleanup controller would add substantial storage-specific lifecycle responsibility and risk deleting valuable data; require explicit ownership and retention contracts before considering it.

docs.title: 31.1 · Explain the effective resource envelope in offline plans
docs.text: Partially implemented. Same shared resource summary as reviews18/19; value-provenance/conflict annotations remain unimplemented. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 31.2 · Add an on-demand Spark performance evidence report
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Capacity requests are delivered. On-demand Spark performance collection needs event-log authorization and data-volume limits distinct from pod diagnostics.

Required evidence before implementation: Against small known workloads and REST fixtures, the report identifies the expected slow stage and matches the source quantities. Attempt selection, missing metrics, timeouts, and truncation produce explicit partial reports rather than misleading zero values.

Feedback: Keep infrastructure health and workload efficiency visibly separate. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid universal tuning presets or automatic memory increases. Heap, overhead, partitioning, skew, and concurrency interact with workload and data shape. A preset labeled optimized would hide that uncertainty. Prefer explicit evidence, reproducible profile comparisons, and changes users can inspect; do not infer optimal settings from pod success or one OOM event.

docs.title: 32.1 · Bounded fleet canary checks with latency reporting
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Cleanup semantics are fixed. Multi-endpoint canaries and draining recipes need a selected shared-server service contract.

Required evidence before implementation: For five fixture endpoints with one stalled endpoint, emit five attributable results within the configured overall deadline, never exceed the concurrency cap, preserve healthy results, and expose no token values. A scheduled staging trial must demonstrate the documented maximum probe rate.

docs.title: 32.2 · Staging qualification recipe for session expiry and endpoint maintenance
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Cleanup semantics are fixed. Multi-endpoint canaries and draining recipes need a selected shared-server service contract.

Required evidence before implementation: Against a disposable staging service, record client termination and new-session recovery times, verify the configured cleanup objective using the operator’s server evidence, and mark unavailable server evidence as unverified rather than passing. Confirm the client harness itself exits within its deadline.

Feedback: Describe session cleanup as an attempted release, with explicit failure semantics. Cleanup no longer masks an application failure; cleanup-only failure remains visible. Tests cover both paths, and the first notebook example uses generated data. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid turning the companion into a full Connect service platform. Server pools, session routing, admission queues, tenant identity, and autoscaling introduce a new operational product. Keep these with the existing service owner and improve observable integration boundaries first; client profiles and shared tokens cannot establish capacity control or tenant isolation.

docs.title: 33.1 · Persist the submission receipt before entering a long wait
docs.text: Implemented. Atomic no-overwrite receipt file is published before waiting and survives observation failure. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 33.2 · Extend machine-readable contracts to explicit cleanup commands
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Early receipts and guarded cancellation are delivered. General structured cleanup results remain separate from accepted cancellation and garbage-collection observation.

Required evidence before implementation: A cleanup shell fixture must parse one JSON document for success, missing application, and API failure; verify consistent exit codes, opt-in already-absent success, and preserved --force behavior. Neither command should require parsing human text.

Feedback: Publish an explicit command-by-command automation contract matrix. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid maintaining a separate workflow engine or CI-provider SDK. Stable receipts, explicit action results, and small shell examples can serve several CI systems through existing commands. Provider-specific orchestration, automatic retries, and implicit cancellation policies would add maintenance and ambiguous ownership without evidence here that the shared CLI is insufficient.

docs.title: 34.1 · Publish a typed public SDK boundary with compatibility fixtures
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Supported imports/sharing semantics are documented. A new facade or complete exception taxonomy needs a backward-compatible migration proposal.

Required evidence before implementation: A small downstream fixture type-checks successful local, remote, and SQL usage; misspelled keywords and reading a plan-only field from a submission result fail statically. The same fixture imports from an installed wheel without optional Airflow or Connect packages.

docs.title: 34.2 · Make SDK failure categories programmatic and backward compatible
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Supported imports/sharing semantics are documented. A new facade or complete exception taxonomy needs a backward-compatible migration proposal.

Required evidence before implementation: Consumer fixtures branch by category without parsing messages; existing exception catches still work; a local wait timeout includes the submitted identity; a remote transport failure reports uncertainty without inventing a run identity.

Feedback: Clarify client sharing before consumers assume reentrant submission. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid mirroring the entire SDK with an async implementation. An async twin would double public signatures, error guarantees, and maintenance before concrete integration demand is established. First publish blocking and cancellation semantics, stabilize value/error contracts, and document that cancelling a waiting caller does not cancel its Spark application.

docs.title: 35.1 · Validate the whole environment matrix and explain promotion differences
docs.text: Implemented bounded scope. Base plus every named profile can be validated offline in one command. A semantic promotion diff remains a separate candidate. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 35.2 · Bind submission to an approved source receipt
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. All-profile validation is delivered. Provenance receipts and semantic promotion diffs need canonicalization and secret-handling design before claiming approval integrity.

Required evidence before implementation: An unchanged checkout and template pass receipt verification. Changing one template byte, the selected profile, or the package version rejects submission before resource creation. The ordinary unguarded workflow remains available.

Feedback: Make the production example select its cluster explicitly. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid a new GitOps controller for transient Spark resources. Do not turn illustrative plans into continuously reconciled manifests. That would introduce workload ownership, duplicate-run, deletion, and reconciliation semantics beyond this SDK. Keep configuration review and promotion integration small, and leave trigger ownership with existing orchestration tools. The documentation already correctly explains why preview resources are not directly applicable.

docs.title: 36.1 · Make Helm values a validated configuration contract
docs.text: Implemented bounded scope. Chart schema validates maintained chart controls and render tests cover valid/invalid inputs; arbitrary Kubernetes maps remain escape hatches. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 36.2 · Separate service-account and RBAC ownership for existing clusters
docs.text:
Implemented bounded scope. External service-account/RBAC ownership is represented explicitly and documented; no new infrastructure provider. Implementation or contract.

Feedback: Avoid mutable image defaults in reproducible chart upgrades. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Do not build a dedicated Terraform provider yet. A maintained Helm contract and a short integration example cover installation ownership without adding provider releases, state migrations, credential handling, and another public API. Revisit only if concrete lifecycle requirements cannot be expressed through existing Kubernetes and Helm resources.

docs.title: 37.1 · Add a conservative SparkApplication migration assessor and importer
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Client versus controller ownership is clarified. A Spark Operator importer requires real manifests and must report every unsupported semantic; no silent conversion.

Required evidence before implementation: For a small published fixture corpus, every source leaf has an explicit accounting status; supported fixtures produce validated jobs and expected plans; a fixture containing an unsupported lifecycle setting cannot receive a migration-ready result.

docs.title: 37.2 · Provide a bounded parity report for side-by-side migration trials
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Client versus controller ownership is clarified. A Spark Operator importer requires real manifests and must report every unsupported semantic; no silent conversion.

Required evidence before implementation: Reference fixtures detect an omitted volume, a service-account change, and a resource change while ignoring generated identifiers. Redacted values produce unverifiable results, never false equality. A maintainer can complete the paired-run checklist without changing an existing controller-managed workload.

Feedback: State the lifecycle ownership change before presenting portable YAML. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid building a second SparkApplication reconciler. Controller compatibility would expand lifecycle, upgrade, and CRD obligations substantially. Start with explicit migration assessment and comparison; preserve the ability to retain an existing operator for workloads whose lifecycle requirements do not fit direct submission.

docs.title: 38.1 · Expose a framework-neutral run outcome helper
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Shared receipt and lifecycle contracts are documented. A Dagster/Prefect adapter needs an adopter and interruption-recovery tests instead of copied Airflow operators.

Required evidence before implementation: A shared fixture suite exercises successful, failed, missing, unknown, and timed-out runs. The helper and CLI agree on workload classification; a sample wrapper cannot report a failed or unknown workload as success and does not delete a job after observation timeout.

docs.title: 38.2 · Publish restart-aware Dagster and Prefect integration recipes
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Shared receipt and lifecycle contracts are documented. A Dagster/Prefect adapter needs an adopter and interruption-recovery tests instead of copied Airflow operators.

Required evidence before implementation: Restart each example after handle persistence and verify that it observes the original pod without creating another. A terminal successful run remains successful on retry; API unavailability does not trigger resubmission. Document and exercise the uncertain-submission branch.

Feedback: Make lifecycle policy differences visible to adapter authors. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid cloning the Airflow operator into two new providers. Large dedicated adapters would multiply submission, cleanup, UI-link, and outcome-policy maintenance before demand is established. Start with shared SDK primitives and narrow runnable recipes; promote them into optional packages only when actual framework-specific requirements justify ownership.

docs.title: 39.1 · Ship thin Argo and Kubeflow submit-and-observe examples
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Early receipts support workflow handoff. A maintained Argo/Kubeflow example needs an actual target workflow and cache/retry policy.

Required evidence before implementation: Run a tiny successful and failing job through both examples. Downstream work starts only after success; failure is visible; retrying the observer preserves the original application ID; the receipt and declared data URI reach the downstream task.

docs.title: 39.2 · Persist a run receipt before a long observation step begins
docs.text:
Implemented. Shared early receipt mechanism supports interrupted workflow workers; it cannot recover an unknown submission response. Implementation or contract.

Feedback: Make pipeline side effects and completion semantics explicit. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid introducing an orchestrator-specific controller. Argo and Kubeflow already own DAG execution and retries. Another controller would add lifecycle and compatibility obligations before thin CLI components establish adoption. Keep scheduling in the workflow engine and Spark submission/observation in the existing shared implementation.

docs.title: 40.1 · Add a tested OpenLineage recipe using existing job profiles
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Operational history is explicitly not lineage. OpenLineage and retained task correlation need a chosen endpoint, event semantics and privacy policy.

Required evidence before implementation: The fixture produces captured upstream events containing the expected input/output datasets, stable logical job identity, and supplied parent identity; a second execution has a distinct run identity. The uninstrumented starter remains usable.

docs.title: 40.2 · Retain opt-in orchestration correlation in recorded runs
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Operational history is explicitly not lineage. OpenLineage and retained task correlation need a chosen endpoint, event semantics and privacy policy.

Required evidence before implementation: Record an operator-created pod, remove it, and confirm its DAG/run/task/mapping/submission-attempt association remains available. Disabled collection retains none of those fields; invalid context is omitted; unrelated annotations never enter storage.

Feedback: Keep operational observations distinct from lineage completion. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid building a parallel lineage engine from pod polling. Pod metadata cannot reveal reliable dataset reads, writes, or commit semantics. Delegate those facts to upstream instrumentation and existing catalogs; use this project for configuration and correlation. A second event collector, catalog, or lineage graph would expand maintenance while offering weaker evidence.

docs.title: 41.1 · Add explicit rejection budgets before publishing ETL outputs
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Quarantine precedence and SQL assertion guidance are documented. Reject budgets/quality-check APIs need explicit data correctness and rollback contracts.

Required evidence before implementation: Against pre-existing output fixtures, an all-invalid batch and an over-budget batch fail without changing clean_orders or daily_revenue; the configured boundary passes; empty input has a documented outcome; the current accepted fixture retains its verified results.

docs.title: 41.2 · Offer named SQL quality checks with strict result semantics
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Quarantine precedence and SQL assertion guidance are documented. Reject budgets/quality-check APIs need explicit data correctness and rollback contracts.

Required evidence before implementation: One passing check completes; false, null, zero-row, multi-row, and SQL-error cases fail with the named check; a normal SELECT that returns false remains unchanged outside check mode; summaries never contain sampled dataset rows.

Feedback: Make the quarantine explanation complete enough to diagnose upstream faults. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Do not label Kubernetes success as certified data quality. The UI accurately describes recorded status as the last observed phase at frontend/src/Runs.tsx:107. Preserve that boundary: missing quality evidence means unknown, not passed. Avoid adding a built-in quality platform when explicit application checks and small reusable conventions address the immediate need.

docs.title: 42.1 · Add a bounded submission-key and receipt reconciliation contract
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. UID cancellation and partial identity are implemented. A durable idempotency ledger needs atomic reservation, fingerprints, reconciliation and retention design.

Required evidence before implementation: Inject a lost HTTP response after driver creation, restart the API, and issue ten concurrent replays: all resolve to one driver UID. A changed document conflicts. A replay after driver deletion cannot create another driver within the published retention window.

docs.title: 42.2 · Make cancellation target an immutable run identity
docs.text:
Partially implemented. UID-bearing handles and guarded cancellation reject replaced/wrong-role drivers. Bounded disappearance observation and an already-gone result are not implemented; accepted deletion is distinct from completed cleanup. Implementation or contract.

Feedback: Expose partial-submission identity before declaring submission failure. The client records confirmed driver identity immediately after creation and exposes submission phase; CLI can persist a partial receipt. An ambiguous create response remains unknown and is never blindly retried. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Do not add blanket transport retries or an exactly-once marketing claim. Transport uncertainty is not proof of failed submission. Repeated POSTs currently generate different run identities, and even a future durable submission key would only deduplicate job creation, not application side effects or externally triggered reruns.

docs.title: 43.1 · Exercise public startup deadlines against a deliberately unschedulable driver
docs.text: Implemented. Client and both Airflow profiles exercise unschedulable-driver observation/startup deadlines on disposable Kubernetes. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 43.2 · Add one packaged browser-to-Kubernetes log failure contract
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Real client/Airflow fault tests are expanded without multiplying all combinations. Browser-to-real-cluster streaming remains a separate fixture with gateway setup.

Required evidence before implementation: The browser receives the real sentinel through the packaged server without routeWebSocket interception; driver deletion yields the specified terminal/error state within a bounded interval; reopening cannot display data from the closed connection. Failure artifacts include browser trace, server logs, and cluster diagnostics.

Feedback: Persist scenario outcomes before advancing to the next case. Client scenario outcomes are persisted after each attempt, including failure category, while preserving the failing process exit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid multiplying every fault across every supported version. The existing runtime matrix already exercises three Spark releases. Initially run deterministic lifecycle faults on one representative stack; expand only when version-dependent evidence justifies it. Random pod/node destruction and blanket retries would make failures harder to interpret while consuming the maintainers’ CI budget.

docs.title: 44.1 · Require release eligibility evidence for the tagged commit
docs.text: Implemented. Exact-tag workflow eligibility gate, nonpublishing validation and artifact-version evidence before publication. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 44.2 · Define a small supported surface and a practical deprecation rule
docs.text:
Documented. Documented public boundaries, compatibility expectations and support scope; no indefinite enterprise SLA. Implementation or contract.

Feedback: Make the roadmap express choices rather than open-ended promises. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid automatic feature parity across every integration. TODO asks both the CLI and Airflow operator to support all Python-client features. Treat parity as a deliberate choice: some capabilities belong only in the SDK or existing configuration escape hatches. Requiring every new capability in every surface multiplies documentation, compatibility, and review obligations for a small maintenance team. Build an adapter only when a concrete workflow justifies it.

docs.title: 45.1 · Add a start-here route map with prerequisite checkpoints
docs.text: Documented. A start-here route selector links canonical existing paths rather than duplicating installation instructions. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 45.2 · Turn diagnostics documentation into an evidence-first troubleshooting path
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Canonical navigation is delivered; operational guidance links existing diagnostics. No second tutorial framework is introduced.

Required evidence before implementation: Using four scripted scenarios, an unfamiliar reader selects the intended next inspection step in at least three cases and correctly explains that empty or incomplete diagnostics do not prove health in both relevant scenarios.

Feedback: Reduce duplicated installation and getting-started instructions. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid a second tutorial framework or a broad documentation rewrite. The repository already has tested examples and precise technical guides. A small navigation layer, focused troubleshooting guidance, and fewer duplicated commands offer a more maintainable learning improvement than a new example suite, documentation portal, or speculative beginner curriculum. Validate discovery friction before expanding scope.

docs.title: 46.1 · Preserve keyboard orientation when embedded views change
docs.text: Implemented. Embedded navigation moves focus deliberately; workload quick links include identity. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 46.2 · Offer a stable reading snapshot for streaming logs
docs.text:
Implemented. Reading can freeze a bounded log snapshot independently of continuing collection. Implementation or contract.

Feedback: Keep the semantic table, but make repeated quick links identifiable. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Do not announce the entire live log stream. Adding an assertive live region to the changing log text would create continuous speech and compete with navigation and error messages. Prefer stable user-controlled reading and sparse state summaries; do not infer accessibility conformance from automated role checks alone.

docs.title: 47.1 · Make snapshot freshness visible where operators inspect and act
docs.text: Implemented. Shared views show successful-fetch age and the intentional pause during detail inspection. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 47.2 · Give diagnostics a compact triage summary with expandable evidence
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Severity overview, collapsible evidence and prioritization remain separate candidates. Freshness is delivered under47.1.

Required evidence before implementation: In paired usability tasks using the same twelve-finding report, target a 25% reduction in median time to locate the highest-severity finding and its next step, without reducing correct interpretation of incomplete evidence. Verify keyboard access to every finding and evidence section.

Feedback: Keep the existing confirmation safeguards, but always show the target identity. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid presenting retained snapshots as definitive reliability or duration analytics. The recorder can miss entire short-lived runs and unobserved transitions, and disappearance does not establish an outcome (docs/user-guide/run-history.md:56–60). Attractive success-rate or exact-duration charts would imply a completeness the data does not provide. Favor explicit observation semantics until an appropriate event source and interpretation are established.

docs.title: 48.1 · Publish one reproducible deployment recipe per release
docs.text: Foundation only. Release evidence ties package artifacts, image inputs and eligibility to a commit; deployment guide records the selected chart/image combination. Real target-cluster qualification remains required. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 48.2 · Provide a rehearsable upgrade and recovery exercise for the single-pod deployment
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Release/deployment evidence is delivered. A destructive upgrade/restore exercise needs a selected supported deployment and explicit data/recovery fixture.

Required evidence before implementation: An engineer who did not write the runbook completes the drill on staging, restores the chosen checkpoint's run UIDs, and records downtime and recovery time without undocumented steps. The team can make an explicit acceptance decision against its own service target.

Feedback: Make the support boundary as precise as the deployment boundaries. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Do not build an enterprise control plane to satisfy an evaluation checklist. Adding tenant identity, HA databases, proprietary support workflows, and policy administration at once would expand the ownership burden for maintainers and the small teams evaluating the project. First make the existing bounded deployment reproducible, recoverable, and explicit about support; reject adoption scenarios whose requirements exceed those boundaries.

docs.title: 49.1 · Add a project-fit landing page with outcome-based entry paths
docs.text: Documented. Start-here explains project fit and routes to existing examples. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 49.2 · Offer a first-contribution pathway with bounded review contracts
docs.text:
Partially documented. Contributor guidance, scoped roadmap and repository skills describe concrete entry points and checks. Implementation or contract.

Feedback: Replace stale roadmap promises with scoped, current opportunities. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Avoid an integration-logo collection without maintained user journeys. Adding badges, superficial scheduler adapters or many nearly identical demos would increase the perceived support surface without proving adoption value. Prefer a few verifiable outcomes using the existing SDK, CLI, shared UI and starters, and label unverified ecosystem combinations explicitly.

docs.title: 50.1 · Ship one reproducible release bundle across package, chart and API image
docs.text: Foundation only. Release artifact evidence and exact-commit gate establish reproducible inputs. A full enterprise-certified bundle is not promised. Implementation or contract.

docs.title: 50.2 · Provide one tested external-gateway recipe for operator access
docs.text:
Not adopted in this change. Release reproducibility is delivered. One actual external gateway needs adoption-driven HTTP/WebSocket/identity qualification before becoming a supported deployment recipe.

Required evidence before implementation: The example passes authenticated browser and Airflow requests, streams logs, rejects unauthenticated and forged-identity requests, rejects invalid-CSRF writes, and never exposes the operator token to browser configuration. Direct backend access is blocked in the deployment fixture.

Feedback: Make compatibility retirement criteria part of the product scope. The clarified behavior and ownership boundaries are captured in the linked implementation or canonical guide; existing support limits remain explicit. Response.

Scope caution accepted: Refuse a multi-tenant, highly available Spark control plane. Do not grow operator admission into tenant IAM, the metadata recorder into a distributed database service, or the client into a scheduler. The documented trust-boundary and single-pod limits are coherent product boundaries. Integration requests should first use existing gateways, orchestrators and observability systems; revisit only with concrete users and dedicated maintainers. Those responsibilities would change the project's operating model, not merely add features.

docs.title: Browser and gateway security boundaries
docs.text: The API is an operator tool. The optional remote submission mode uses a shared operator bearer; it does not provide tenant isolation or per-user authorization. A gateway is responsible for authenticating browser users and deciding which users may reach the console. Keep operator credentials out of browser storage, page bootstrap data and WebSocket URLs.

docs.title: Proxy request headers
docs.text:
Spark UI and History Server requests forward only the existing content-negotiation, cache-validation, range and content-type header allowlist, regardless of whether remote submission is enabled. Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization, custom identity headers and arbitrary tracing headers are not forwarded to those upstream services.

This changes the previous behavior of deployments with remote submission disabled. Deployments that relied on implicit gateway credential forwarding must arrange upstream authentication explicitly outside this proxy; there is no arbitrary-header forwarding override. These controls do not isolate untrusted Spark or History HTML from the console's browser origin. Operate those upstream services within the same trust boundary.

docs.title: Mounted Spark UI paths
docs.text:
For a deployment mounted at a path such as /platform/spark, configure the ASGI server's root_path. The proxy keeps Spark UI and History Server links under that prefix, including links generated by upstream HTML with an unprefixed proxyBase. It rewrites only quoted paths for the requested proxy target.

Mounted HTML responses are buffered before delivery, with an 8 MiB decoded limit. Unencoded, identity, gzip and deflate bodies are supported. Oversized, unsupported or malformed compressed HTML returns HTTP 502 before a partial page is sent. Non-HTML responses and deployments without a path prefix keep their streaming behavior.

docs.title: Log WebSocket browser origins
docs.text:
SPARK_ON_K8S_API_WEBSOCKET_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is a comma-separated list of exact public HTTP(S) origins, for example:

export SPARK_ON_K8S_API_WEBSOCKET_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://spark.example.com,https://spark-admin.example.com:8443

Use only scheme, hostname and optional port: no path, trailing slash, query, fragment, credentials or wildcard. Default HTTP and HTTPS ports are equivalent to their explicit forms. If any configured entry is malformed, browser connections are rejected.

With an empty setting, a browser Origin must match the direct request Host and scheme (ws maps to http, wss to https). The application does not consult Forwarded or X-Forwarded-* headers for this decision. The ASGI server's trusted-proxy configuration still controls its request scope; configure that trust narrowly. For a gateway that changes Host or terminates TLS, set the explicit external origin list. A configured list replaces the direct-origin default.

A deployment prefix such as /platform/spark belongs in the server's root_path, never in an origin. The same origin policy applies with or without that prefix. Null, malformed and duplicate Origin headers are rejected before accepting the socket or querying Kubernetes, including when bearer authentication succeeds.

Non-browser clients may omit Origin. This preserves CLI clients and is not an authentication exemption: remote-mode bearer checks still apply. Origin is a browser request boundary, not proof of identity, and non-browser clients can supply it themselves. Gateways should also enforce the intended browser origins, restrict public access and rate-limit upgrades. This policy applies to the log WebSocket route; it does not claim general CSRF protection.

class ExecutorInstances:

        initial: Initial number of executors. If max and min are not provided, defaults to 2,

        scheduler_backlog_timeout: Scheduler backlog timeout to use for dynamic allocation.

        sustained_scheduler_backlog_timeout: Sustained scheduler backlog timeout to use for

class SparkOnK8S(LoggingMixin):
    """Client for submitting Spark apps to Kubernetes

    Examples:
        >>> from spark_on_k8s.client import SparkOnK8S
        >>> spark = SparkOnK8S()
        >>> spark.submit_app(
        ...     image="husseinawala/spark:v3.5.0",
        ...     app_path="local:///opt/spark/examples/jars/spark-examples_2.12-3.5.0.jar",
        ...     class_name="org.apache.spark.examples.SparkPi",
        ...     app_name="spark-pi",
        ...     app_arguments=["1000"],
        ...     namespace="spark",
        ...     service_account="spark",
        ...     app_waiter="log",
        ... )

    Args:
        k8s_client_manager: Kubernetes client manager to use for creating Kubernetes clients
        logger_name: Name of the logger to use for logging, defaults to "SparkOnK8S"
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        k8s_client_manager: KubernetesClientManager | None = None,
        logger_name: str | None = None,
    ):
        super().__init__(logger_name=logger_name or "SparkOnK8S")
        self.k8s_client_manager = k8s_client_manager or KubernetesClientManager()
        self.last_submitted_app_id: str | None = None
        self.last_submitted_run: RunHandle | None = None
        self.last_submission_phase: str | None = None
        self.app_manager = SparkAppManager(k8s_client_manager=self.k8s_client_manager)

    def submit_run(self, **kwargs) -> RunHandle:
        """Submit using the same arguments as submit_app, returning a structured run identity."""
        if kwargs.get("dry_run"):
            raise ValueError("submit_run requires a real submission and does not support dry_run")
        self.submit_app(**kwargs)
        if self.last_submitted_run is None:
            raise RuntimeError("Submission completed without a run identity")
        return self.last_submitted_run

    def create_connect_server(self, config: ConnectServerConfig) -> ConnectServerHandle:
        """Create a private Spark Connect server; return identity before checking readiness."""
        from spark_on_k8s.connect_server import create_connect_server

        return create_connect_server(self, config)

    def connect_server_status(self, handle: ConnectServerHandle, *, timeout: float = 10) -> dict:
        """Observe exactly the recorded server resources without importing PySpark."""
        from spark_on_k8s.connect_server import connect_server_status

        return connect_server_status(self, handle, timeout=timeout)

    def wait_connect_server_ready(
        self,
        handle: ConnectServerHandle,
        *,
        profile: ConnectProfile,
        timeout: float = 60,
        poll_interval: float = 1,
    ) -> dict:
        """Verify a real Connect query, remote application identity and current resource UIDs."""
        from spark_on_k8s.connect_server import wait_connect_server_ready

        return wait_connect_server_ready(
            self, handle, profile=profile, timeout=timeout, poll_interval=poll_interval
        )

    def delete_connect_server(self, handle: ConnectServerHandle, *, timeout: float = 10) -> dict:
        """Request deletion only after validating all recorded server resource identities."""
        from spark_on_k8s.connect_server import delete_connect_server

        return delete_connect_server(self, handle, timeout=timeout)

    def submit_sql(
        self,
        *,
        sql: str | None = None,
        sql_file: str | Path | None = None,
        **submit_options: Any,
    ) -> str | ApplicationPlan:
        """Submit inline SQL or a local SQL file using a PySpark image.

        Exactly one of ``sql`` and ``sql_file`` is required. Other keyword arguments
        are passed to :meth:`submit_app`, including image, resources, namespace,
        service account, packages, and waiter options. SQL runs in statement order;
        the first failed statement fails the application. This is not a transaction.
        Set ``dry_run=True`` to return an offline :class:`ApplicationPlan` instead of submitting.

        from spark_on_k8s.sql import prepare_sql_options

    def diagnose_app(
        self,
        *,
        namespace: str,
        app_id: str | None = None,
        pod_name: str | None = None,
        pod_limit: int = 20,
        event_limit: int = 100,
        timeout: float = 10,
    ):
        """Read bounded pod/event evidence without changing the application."""
        from spark_on_k8s.diagnostics import _limits, collect_diagnosis, validate_target

        if (app_id is None) == (pod_name is None):
            raise ValueError("Provide exactly one of app_id or pod_name")
        validate_target(namespace, app_id if app_id is not None else pod_name, label=app_id is not None)
        deadline = _limits(pod_limit, event_limit, timeout)
        with self.k8s_client_manager.client() as client:
            api = k8s.CoreV1Api(client)
            if pod_name is not None:
                driver = api.read_namespaced_pod(
                    namespace=namespace, name=pod_name, **deadline.request_options()
                )
            else:
                response = api.list_namespaced_pod(
                    namespace=namespace,
                    label_selector=f"spark-role=driver,spark-app-id={app_id}",
                    limit=2,
                    **deadline.request_options(),
                )
                if len(response.items) != 1:
                    raise ValueError("Expected one Spark driver; use pod_name to select an existing driver")
                driver = response.items[0]
            return collect_diagnosis(
                api,
                driver,
                namespace=namespace,
                pod_limit=pod_limit,
                event_limit=event_limit,
                timeout=deadline.remaining(),
            )

    def doctor(self, *, namespace: str, service_account: str = "spark", timeout: float = 10):
        """Check caller access and driver service-account existence without applying changes."""
        from spark_on_k8s.doctor import check_cluster

        with self.k8s_client_manager.client() as client:
            return check_cluster(
                client, namespace=namespace, service_account=service_account, timeout=timeout
            )

    def _process_executor_template(self, executor_template: str) -> str:
        """Process executor template string, reading from file if it's a file path.

        Args:
            executor_template: Either template content as string or path to template file

        Returns:
            Template content as string

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the resulting content is not valid YAML
        """
        # Try to read from file first, if that fails use the string as-is
        try:
            template_path = Path(executor_template).expanduser()
            content = template_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except (OSError, PermissionError):
            # Not a valid file path, use as content
            content = executor_template

        # Validate that the content is valid YAML and expected Kubernetes resource
        try:
            parsed = yaml.safe_load(content)
        except yaml.YAMLError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"Executor template contains invalid YAML: {e}") from e

        # Check if it's a proper Kubernetes resource structure
        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            raise ValueError("Executor template must be a Kubernetes resource (YAML object)")

        if parsed.get("kind") != "Pod":
            raise ValueError("Executor template must be a Kubernetes Pod resource (kind: Pod)")

        return content

                )

                configmap_mount_path = all_configmaps[ind]["mount_path"]
                driver_volume_mounts.append(
                    k8s.V1VolumeMount(
                        name=configmap.metadata.name,
                        mount_path=configmap_mount_path,
                    )
                )
        else:
            application_configmaps_volumes = []

        pod = SparkAppManager.create_spark_pod_spec(
            app_name=app_name,
            app_id=app_id,
            image=image,
            image_pull_policy=image_pull_policy,
            namespace=namespace,
            service_account=service_account,
            args=driver_command_args,
            env_variables=driver_environment,
            extra_labels={
                **{key: value for key, value in driver_labels.items() if key != "spark-ui-proxy"},
                **extra_labels,
                "spark-app-name": app_name,
                "spark-app-id": app_id,
                "spark-role": "driver",
            },
            annotations=driver_annotations,
            pod_resources={
                "requests": {
                    "cpu": f"{driver_resources.cpu}",
                    "memory": f"{driver_resources.memory + driver_resources.memory_overhead}Mi",
                },
                "limits": {
                    "cpu": f"{driver_resources.cpu}",
                    "memory": f"{driver_resources.memory + driver_resources.memory_overhead}Mi",
                },
            },
            env_from_secrets=env_from_secrets,
            volumes=volumes,
            volume_mounts=driver_volume_mounts,
            node_selector=driver_node_selector,
            tolerations=driver_tolerations,
            init_containers=driver_init_containers,
            host_aliases=driver_host_aliases,
        )
        if template is not None:
            pod = merge_driver_pod_template(pod, template, driver_container_name)
        if dry_run:
            objects = [("ConfigMap", item) for item in application_configmaps_volumes]
            if secret_values:
                objects.insert(
                    0,
                    (
                        "Secret",
                        self.app_manager.create_secret_object(
                            app_name=app_name,
                            app_id=app_id,
                            secrets_values=secret_values,
                            namespace=namespace,
                        ),
                    ),
                )
            objects.extend(
                [
                    ("Pod", pod),
                    (
                        "Service",
                        SparkAppManager.create_headless_service_object(
                            app_name=app_name, app_id=app_id, namespace=namespace, extra_labels=extra_labels
                        ),
                    ),
                ]
            )
            with k8s.ApiClient() as serializer:
                resources = tuple(
                    {**serializer.sanitize_for_serialization(item), "apiVersion": "v1", "kind": kind}
                    for kind, item in objects
                )
            pod_name = pod["metadata"]["name"] if isinstance(pod, dict) else pod.metadata.name
            from spark_on_k8s.resource_plan import resource_envelope

            planned_pod = next(item for item in resources if item["kind"] == "Pod")
            return ApplicationPlan(
                namespace,
                app_id,
                pod_name,
                resources,
                resource_envelope(planned_pod, {**basic_conf, **spark_conf}),
            )
        self.last_submission_phase = "creating_resources"
        with self.k8s_client_manager.client() as client:
            api = k8s.CoreV1Api(client)
            if secret_values:
                application_secret = self.app_manager.create_secret_object(
                    app_name=app_name,
                    app_id=app_id,
                    secrets_values=secret_values,
                    namespace=namespace,
                )
                api.create_namespaced_secret(namespace=namespace, body=application_secret)
            for configmap in application_configmaps_volumes:
                api.create_namespaced_config_map(namespace=namespace, body=configmap)
            pod = api.create_namespaced_pod(
                namespace=namespace,
                body=pod,
            )
            # Preserve the confirmed driver identity before later resource operations can fail.
            self.last_submitted_app_id = app_id
            self.last_submitted_run = RunHandle(
                namespace=namespace, app_id=app_id, driver_pod=pod.metadata.name, driver_uid=pod.metadata.uid
            )
            self.last_submission_phase = "driver_created"
            if secret_values:
                application_secret.metadata.owner_references = [
                    k8s.V1OwnerReference(
                        api_version="v1",
                        kind="Pod",
                        name=pod.metadata.name,
                        uid=pod.metadata.uid,
                    )
                ]
                api.patch_namespaced_secret(
                    namespace=namespace,
                    name=application_secret.metadata.name,
                    body=application_secret,
                )
            for configmap in application_configmaps_volumes:
                configmap.metadata.owner_references = [
                    k8s.V1OwnerReference(
                        api_version="v1",
                        kind="Pod",
                        name=pod.metadata.name,
                        uid=pod.metadata.uid,
                    )
                ]
                api.patch_namespaced_config_map(
                    namespace=namespace,
                    name=configmap.metadata.name,
                    body=configmap,
                )
            api.create_namespaced_service(
                namespace=namespace,
                body=SparkAppManager.create_headless_service_object(
                    app_name=app_name,
                    app_id=app_id,
                    namespace=namespace,
                    pod_owner_uid=pod.metadata.uid,
                    extra_labels=extra_labels,
                ),
            )
        self.last_submission_phase = "resources_created"
        deadline = WaitDeadline(wait_timeout)
        if app_waiter == SparkAppWait.LOG:
            self.app_manager.stream_logs(
                namespace=namespace,
                pod_name=pod.metadata.name,
                startup_timeout=startup_timeout,
                should_print=should_print,
                **({"timeout": deadline.remaining()} if wait_timeout is not None else {}),
            )
        if app_waiter == SparkAppWait.WAIT or (app_waiter == SparkAppWait.LOG and wait_timeout is not None):
            self.app_manager.wait_for_app(
                namespace=namespace,
                pod_name=pod.metadata.name,
                poll_interval=5,
                startup_timeout=startup_timeout,
                should_print=should_print,
                **({"timeout": deadline.remaining()} if wait_timeout is not None else {}),
            )
        return pod.metadata.name

    def cancel_run(self, run: RunHandle, *, force: bool = False) -> None:
        """Request deletion of exactly the recorded driver; does not wait for cleanup."""
        self.app_manager.cancel_run(run, force=force)

    def plan_app(self, **kwargs) -> ApplicationPlan:
        """Render a deterministic offline preview using the same builder as submission."""
        kwargs.setdefault("app_id_suffix", lambda: "-preview")
        kwargs["dry_run"] = True
        kwargs["should_print"] = False
        result = self.submit_app(**kwargs)
        assert isinstance(result, ApplicationPlan)
        return result

    def _parse_app_name_and_id(
        self,
        *,
        app_name: str | None = None,
        app_id_suffix: Callable[[], str] = default_app_id_suffix,
        should_print: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """Parse the application name and ID

        This function will generate a valid application name and ID from the provided application name.
            It will ensure that the application name and ID respect the Kubernetes naming conventions
            (e.g. no uppercase characters, no
        special characters, start with a letter, etc.), and they are not too long
            (less than 64 characters for service
        names and labels values).

        Args:
            app_name: Name of the Spark application
            app_id_suffix: Function to generate a suffix for the application ID,
                defaults to `default_app_id_suffix`
            should_print: Whether to print logs instead of logging them, defaults to False

        Returns:
            Tuple of the application name and ID
        """
        if not app_name:
            app_name = f"spark-app{app_id_suffix()}"
            app_id = app_name
        else:
            original_app_name = app_name
            # All to lowercase
            app_name = app_name.lower()
            app_id_suffix_str = app_id_suffix()
            # Maximum length for pod labels and service names is 63 characters
            if len(app_name) > (63 - len(app_id_suffix_str)):
                app_name = app_name[: (63 - len(app_id_suffix_str))]
            # Replace all non-alphanumeric characters with dashes
            app_name = re.sub(r"[^0-9a-zA-Z]+", "-", app_name)
            # Remove leading non-alphabetic characters
            app_name = re.sub(r"^[^a-zA-Z]*", "", app_name)
            # Remove trailing dashes
            app_name = re.sub(r"-*$", "", app_name)
            app_id = app_name + app_id_suffix_str
            if app_name != original_app_name:
                self.log(
                    msg=(
                        f"Application name {original_app_name!r} has been sanitized"
                        f" to {app_name!r} to comply with Kubernetes naming conventions"
                    ),
                    level=logging.WARNING,
                    should_print=should_print,
                )
        return app_name, app_id

    @staticmethod
    def _value_to_str(value: Any) -> str:
        if isinstance(value, bool):
            return str(value).lower()
        return str(value)

    @staticmethod
    def _driver_environment(spark_conf: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Apply driver environment properties before this client creates the Pod."""
        prefix = "spark.kubernetes.driverEnv."
        environment = {}
        for key, value in spark_conf.items():
            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.startswith(prefix):
                continue
            name = key.removeprefix(prefix)
            if not name or any(ord(char) < 32 or ord(char) > 126 or char == "=" for char in name):
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid driver environment variable name in Spark property {key!r}")
            if name == "SPARK_DRIVER_BIND_ADDRESS":
                raise ValueError(
                    "SPARK_DRIVER_BIND_ADDRESS is managed and cannot be set via Spark properties"
                )
            if not isinstance(value, (str, bool, int, float)) or (
                isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value)
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Driver environment property {key!r} must have a string or finite scalar value"
                )
            rendered = SparkOnK8S._value_to_str(value)
            if "\0" in rendered:
                raise ValueError(f"Driver environment property {key!r} cannot contain NUL")
            environment[name] = rendered
        return environment

    @staticmethod
    def _spark_config_to_arguments(spark_conf: dict[str, str] | None) -> list[str]:
        """Convert Spark configuration to a list of arguments

        Args:
            spark_conf: Spark configuration dictionary

        Returns:
            List of arguments
        """
        if not spark_conf:
            return []
        args = []
        for key, value in spark_conf.items():
            args.extend(["--conf", f"{key}={SparkOnK8S._value_to_str(value)}"])
        return args

    @staticmethod
    def _executor_secrets_config(
        secret_values: dict[str, str] | None,
        app_id: str,
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Spark configuration to load environment variables from the secret

        Args:
            secret_values: Secret values to pass to the application as environment variables
            app_id: Application ID

        Returns:
            Spark configuration dictionary
        """
        if not secret_values:
            return {}
        return {
            f"spark.kubernetes.executor.secretKeyRef.{secret_name}": f"{app_id}:{secret_name}"
            for secret_name in secret_values.keys()
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _executor_volumes_config(
        volumes: list[k8s.V1Volume] | None,
        volume_mounts: list[k8s.V1VolumeMount] | None,
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Spark configuration to mount volumes to the executors

        Args:
            volumes: List of volumes to mount to the driver and/or executors
            volume_mounts: List of volume mounts to mount to the executors

        Returns:
            Spark configuration dictionary
        """
        if not volumes:
            return {}
        config = {}
        # https://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/running-on-kubernetes.html#using-kubernetes-volumes
        supported_volume_types = {
            "hostPath": {"path"},
            "emptyDir": {"medium", "sizeLimit"},
            "nfs": {"path", "server"},
            "persistentVolumeClaim": {"claimName"},
        }
        loaded_volumes = {}
        volumes_config = {}
        read_only_volumes = set()
        for volume in volumes:
            volume_name = volume.name
            volume_mapped_type: str | None = None
            volume_type_str: str | None = None
            for attr in k8s.V1Volume.attribute_map:
                if attr != "name" and getattr(volume, attr) is not None:
                    volume_mapped_type = k8s.V1Volume.attribute_map[attr]
                    volume_type_str = k8s.V1Volume.openapi_types[attr]
                    volume = getattr(volume, attr)
                    break
            if volume_mapped_type not in supported_volume_types:
                continue
            volume_type = getattr(k8s, volume_type_str)
            loaded_volumes[volume_name] = volume_mapped_type
            if getattr(volume, "read_only", False):
                read_only_volumes.add(volume_name)
            volumes_config[volume_name] = {}
            for attr in volume_type.attribute_map:
                option_name = volume_type.attribute_map[attr]
                if (
                    option_name in supported_volume_types[volume_mapped_type]
                    and getattr(volume, attr) is not None
                ):
                    volumes_config[volume_name][
                        f"spark.kubernetes.executor.volumes.{volume_mapped_type}.{volume_name}.options.{option_name}"
                    ] = getattr(volume, attr)
        for volume_mount in volume_mounts:
            if volume_mount.name not in loaded_volumes:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Volume {volume_mount.name} is not found in the volumes list or is not supported.\n"
                    "Please make sure to add the volume to the volumes list and use one of"
                    f" the supported types: {supported_volume_types}"
                )
            config.update(volumes_config[volume_mount.name])
            volume_config_prefix = (
                "spark.kubernetes.executor.volumes."
                f"{loaded_volumes[volume_mount.name]}.{volume_mount.name}.mount"
            )
            config[f"{volume_config_prefix}.path"] = volume_mount.mount_path
            if volume_mount.sub_path:
                config[f"{volume_config_prefix}.subPath"] = volume_mount.sub_path
            if volume_mount.read_only or volume_mount.name in read_only_volumes:
                config[f"{volume_config_prefix}.readOnly"] = True
        return config

    @staticmethod
    def _executor_node_selector(
        node_selector: dict[str, str] | None,
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Spark configuration to set node selector for the executors

        Args:
            node_selector: Node selector for the executors

        Returns:
            Spark configuration dictionary
        """
        if not node_selector:
            return {}
        return {
            f"spark.kubernetes.executor.node.selector.{key}": value for key, value in node_selector.items()
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _executor_labels(
        labels: dict[str, str] | None,
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Spark configuration to set labels for the executors

        Args:
            labels: Labels for the executors

        Returns:
            Spark configuration dictionary
        """
        if not labels:
            return {}
        return {f"spark.kubernetes.executor.label.{key}": value for key, value in labels.items()}

    @staticmethod
    def _executor_annotations(
        annotations: dict[str, str] | None,
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Spark configuration to set annotations for the executors

        Args:
            annotations: Annotations for the executors

        Returns:
            Spark configuration dictionary
        """
        if not annotations:
            return {}
        return {f"spark.kubernetes.executor.annotation.{key}": value for key, value in annotations.items()}

    @staticmethod
    def _executor_pod_template_path(
        executor_pod_template_path: str | None,
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Spark configuration to set the executor pod template file

        Args:
            executor_pod_template_path: Path to the executor pod template file

        Returns:
            Spark configuration dictionary
        """
        if not executor_pod_template_path:
            return {}
        return {"spark.kubernetes.executor.podTemplateFile": executor_pod_template_path}

def diagnose_app(
    self,
    *,
    namespace: str,
    app_id: str | None = None,
    pod_name: str | None = None,
    pod_limit: int = 20,
    event_limit: int = 100,
    timeout: float = 10,
):
    """Read bounded pod/event evidence without changing the application."""
    from spark_on_k8s.diagnostics import _limits, collect_diagnosis, validate_target

    if (app_id is None) == (pod_name is None):
        raise ValueError("Provide exactly one of app_id or pod_name")
    validate_target(namespace, app_id if app_id is not None else pod_name, label=app_id is not None)
    deadline = _limits(pod_limit, event_limit, timeout)
    with self.k8s_client_manager.client() as client:
        api = k8s.CoreV1Api(client)
        if pod_name is not None:
            driver = api.read_namespaced_pod(
                namespace=namespace, name=pod_name, **deadline.request_options()
            )
        else:
            response = api.list_namespaced_pod(
                namespace=namespace,
                label_selector=f"spark-role=driver,spark-app-id={app_id}",
                limit=2,
                **deadline.request_options(),
            )
            if len(response.items) != 1:
                raise ValueError("Expected one Spark driver; use pod_name to select an existing driver")
            driver = response.items[0]
        return collect_diagnosis(
            api,
            driver,
            namespace=namespace,
            pod_limit=pod_limit,
            event_limit=event_limit,
            timeout=deadline.remaining(),
        )
